sentences.text:
Obesh Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 November,
2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Jbp:56062
 1 M
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pramod Kumar Agrawal

On The 7 th Of November, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 46229 of 2025
 Obesh Khan
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Rahul Gupta - Advocate for the applicant.
 Smt. Ranjana Agnihotri - Dy.G.A. for the respondent/S
 Order

This is the first application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail in relation to Crime No.327/2025 registered at Police Station - Junnardeo, District Chhindwara (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B of IPC.

The applicant is in custody since 11.09.2025.
2.

As per the prosecution story, the complainants Manoj Yadav and Vinod Yadav, are the sons of Late Smt. Lalta Bai Yaduvanshi, who had purchased land bearing Survey No. 483/9, area 0.300 hectare, through a registered sale deed dated 06.01.2003.
After her death in 2014, the land remained recorded in her name, and mutation was not carried out in favour of her legal heirs.

During the year 2024, the accused persons Satpal Pal, Indra Singh Chauhan, Malti Jaiswal,
Chandrapal Pawar, Obesh Khan, and Ajesh Suryavanshi allegedly entered into a criminal conspiracy to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:56062 2 MCRC-46229-2025 fraudulently obtain ownership of the said land.

In furtherance of the conspiracy, they are said to have prepared a forged Aadhaar card in the name of Lalita Bai, using the photograph of accused Malti Jaiswal and thereby impersonated the deceased woman to get the land re-registered in the name of co-accused Indra Singh Chauhan before the Sub- Registrar, Junardeo.
On verification, it was found that the forged Aadhaar card bare the same photograph as Malti Jaiswal's genuine card, confirming impersonation and forgery.
Therefore, the offence has been registered against the applicant and co-accused persons under aforesaid offences.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He is in custody since 11.09.2025.
The applicant is not the beneficiary.
There is no criminal antecedents of the applicant.

The conclusion of trial will take Obesh Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159091052/
1 considerable time.

sentences.text: Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be granted bail.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant and has submitted that present applicant knew the fact that real owner of the land Lalita Bai has already expired.
The accused Malti Jaiswal impersonated herself to be Lalita Bai on the basis of forged Aadhar Card and the applicant identified her being the witness.
The applicant has actively participated in the commission of the alleged offence.
Therefore, the applicant does not deserve grant of bail.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6.
Looking to aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, I am not inclined to grant bail to the applicant.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:56062 3 MCRC-46229-2025 7.
Accordingly, present MCRC stands dismissed.
